name: s2-ecology-to-proximity
title: S2 — Ecology to proximity: when does cross-feeding select for persistent contact?
concept: Physical association made operational as encounter rate, adhesion lifetime, diffusion length, and spatial crowding. The two cross-feeding lineages (the S1 community) placed proximate (mixed) vs distant (segregated) along the pore, under varying diffusion — measuring whether the cross-feeding benefit is distance-dependent.
question: When do cross-feeding benefits select for persistent proximity rather than independent coexistence? Does the predicted selection for proximity disappear under high diffusion / well-mixed conditions?
hypothesis: Below a critical diffusion length the cross-feeding flux is distance-dependent and selects for sustained contact; under well-mixed (high-diffusion) conditions the proximity advantage collapses, so selection for contact is a spatial-structure effect, not a given.
claim: Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (low-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding flux is strongly distance-dependent — proximate (mixed) partners sustain the exchange while distant (segregated) partners lose it — creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis. The advantage vanishes under high diffusion (well-mixed), so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.

behavior_tests.name: proximity-selected-under-finite-diffusion
behavior_tests.description: At low diffusion the proximate (mixed) community sustains cross-lineage metabolite flux that a distant (segregated) community loses — so the cross-feeding benefit is distance-dependent and selects for contact. The threshold discriminates mixed (proximate) from the segregated control.

provenance.note: Calibrated at p_diacid=1e-8, p_monoacid=1e-7, k_wash=0.01, k_diffusion=0.001, 250 steps: mixed (proximate) settles to 4.0e-22 (PASS) while the segregated control (the `distant-control` variant) settles to 1.8e-23 (FAIL) — a 22x proximity advantage. Under high diffusion (k_diffusion=0.1) the mixed/segregated ratio falls to 1.26: the advantage vanishes well-mixed.

findings.statement: Calibrated (k_diffusion=0.001, 250 steps): proximate (mixed) partners sustain cross-lineage flux 4.0e-22 mol/tick while distant (segregated) partners sustain only 1.8e-23 — a 22x proximity advantage, so selection favours persistent contact. The advantage is diffusion- dependent: at k_diffusion=0.1 the mixed/segregated ratio is 1.26 (proximity barely matters, diffusion carries the intermediate). Establishes that proximity selection is a spatial- structure effect, not a given — a precondition for intimate symbiosis. Direct in-process run.

literature_anchors.expectation: Asgard protrusions set the length/time scales of transient contact.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: First-fidelity arm: reuses the S1 metabolite-exchange community with placement + diffusion as the proximity lever. settled_cross_lineage_flux (metabolite flux between lineages) is the distance-dependent benefit. The dedicated reaction-diffusion PDE with a continuous separation axis is the next-fidelity arm.
